cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is still preaching to Israel about life in the land the LORD is giving them. And he opens with a hard one. Someone is found killed, lying in a field, and nobody knows who did it.

cards.question: Nobody knows who killed the man in the field. So who has to come out first?

cards.text: So they measure the distance from the body to the towns around it. Friend, I have never measured a thing in my life. I eyeball the chocolate chips, shrug, and call it a recipe.

cards.question: Why do the elders and judges measure from the body to the towns around it?

answers.text: To mark out a grave site

cards.text: Whichever city comes out closest, the job lands on its elders. And they have to bring an animal.

cards.question: The elders of the nearest city take a ___ that has never been yoked or used for work.

cards.text: They lead the heifer down to a valley with running water. It's ground that hasn't been plowed or sown.

cards.question: In that valley, the elders offer the heifer on an altar as a burnt offering.

cards.text: Instead, they break its neck right there by the stream. Then the priests, the sons of Levi, step forward.

cards.question: Why are the priests, the sons of Levi, part of this?

answers.text: God chose them to serve and rule on cases
They live in the city nearest the field
They were the ones who found the victim

cards.text: Then every elder of the nearest city washes his hands in the stream, right over the heifer.

cards.question: As they wash their hands by the stream, the elders declare that they saw who killed the man.

cards.text: They declare that their hands didn't shed this blood and their eyes didn't see it. And they go on, "Accept this atonement, O LORD, for Your people Israel whom You have redeemed, and do not hold the shedding of innocent blood against them."

cards.question: Moses says that after the elders make that declaration, the bloodshed will be atoned for.
With the heifer, the washing and the declaration, Israel purges the ___ of shedding innocent blood from among them.

cards.text: And Moses says that when they do this, they've done what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
Moses moves on to war. When the LORD gives Israel's enemies into their hand and they take captives, a man might see a beautiful woman among them and want her as his wife.
He brings her into his house. But Moses lays out steps that come before any marriage.

cards.question: Once the captive woman is in the man's house, what does Moses say she must do?

answers.text: Shave her head and trim her nails
Learn all the laws of Israel
Serve his family as a maid

cards.text: She also puts aside the clothes she was captured in. Then she gets time in his house to mourn her father and mother.

cards.question: The captive woman lives in his house and mourns her father and mother for a full ___ before he can marry her.

cards.text: Then Moses covers what happens if the man isn't pleased with her.

cards.question: If the man isn't pleased with the woman he married, he's allowed to sell her for money.
The man must let her go wherever she wishes and never treat her as a slave. What reason does Moses give?

answers.text: She came from a royal family
Her people might come for her

cards.text: Next, a man has two wives, one loved and one unloved, and both give him sons. The firstborn son is from the unloved wife.

cards.question: When he divides his inheritance, the man can name the loved wife's son as the firstborn instead.

cards.text: Which wife he loves more doesn't change which son came first. It's like the line at my counter, friend: I might LOVE the baker in the back, but whoever got there first still gets served first.

cards.question: What must the father give the unloved wife's son, his true firstborn?

answers.text: A double portion of all he has
The family house and the land

cards.question: Why does Moses say the right of the firstborn belongs to the unloved wife's son?

answers.text: He's the first son born of his father's strength
His mother was the first wife the man married
He has always been the strongest of the sons

cards.text: Now Moses turns to a heavy one. A son is stubborn and rebellious, and he won't listen to his father and mother, even when they discipline him.

cards.question: The stubborn son's father and mother take hold of him and bring him to the ___ of his city, at the gate of his hometown.

cards.text: At the gate, they tell the elders their son is stubborn and rebellious and won't obey them. Then they add, "He is a glutton and a drunkard."

cards.question: After the parents speak to the elders, what does Moses say happens to the rebellious son?

answers.text: The men of his city stone him
He is sent out of the land
He serves the elders for a year

cards.question: Moses says the rebellious son's case is kept quiet so the rest of Israel never hears about it.

cards.text: Moses says this is how they purge the evil from among them, and all Israel will hear and be afraid. Then the last law in this stretch: a man commits a sin worthy of death, he is executed, and his body is hung on a tree.

cards.question: What must Israel do with the executed man's body hung on the tree?

answers.text: Leave it up for three days
Keep it up until the elders say

cards.question: The body can't stay up overnight, because anyone who is hung on a tree is under God's ___.

cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus, points back to this line later. He writes that Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us (Galatians 3:13).
Moses wraps it up: they must not defile the land the LORD their God is giving them as an inheritance. And friend, this sermon isn't over yet.
